Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Soreness in fingers, cracked skin on palms of hands, worsened in recent weeks; also reports general dryness of skin (legs, not severe).
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began approximately 3–4 months ago; worsening recently to the point of impacting ability to work (absent from work for past 3 days).
- Progression: Increasing pain and dysfunction of hands.
- Location: Palms primarily; some general dryness on legs.
- Associated symptoms: Intermittent itchiness of palms; bleeding only occurs if scratched.
- No associated fever, nausea, vomiting, or bowel/urinary complaints. Appetite and general health otherwise maintained.
- Social history: Works as a hotel housekeeper; frequent exposure to cleaning products; inconsistent use of gloves; recently changed jobs; does not smoke; drinks a couple of pints of alcohol per week.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes.
- Family history: Diabetes; no known family skin problems, asthma, or bowel disease.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented). Previously used E45 cream and antihistamine (names/dose/route/frequency not documented) without benefit.
- Allergies: No known drug or general allergies reported.

Objective:
- No physical examination findings or vital signs documented.
- No investigations performed or results documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Hand dermatitis (cracked, sore, itchy palms in context of occupational exposure):
   - Assessment: Contact dermatitis (likely irritant/contact dermatitis related to cleaning products).
   - Differential diagnosis: None documented.
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Advise strict avoidance of triggers: recommend consistent use of gloves when cleaning.
     - Prescribe topical steroid cream (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Prescribe stronger emollients; advise liberal application 3–4 times daily for next 2 weeks.
     - Patient advised to return for reassessment if symptoms do not improve within 10–14 days, or if symptoms worsen (e.g., spreading, increased dryness).

Quality checks:
●	Missing but clinically expected elements: No documentation of physical examination findings; no detailed description of skin lesions; no medication dosages, names, or specific instructions recorded; allergies confirmed as negative; no documentation of glucose control or diabetes review.
●	Internal conflicts: None noted.
●	Transcript quality: Clear, no significant audio or transcription issues.
